newsitem.title: USA: Ascend climb due to bullish comments, rumors.
newsitem.headline: Ascend climb due to bullish comments, rumors.

text.p: Shares of Ascend Communications Inc have soared 24 percent in the past two days, on positive comments by two Wall Street analysts and on rumors of at least one impending multi-million dollar pact with an Internet service provider, analysts said.

"I heard that Ascend won a big deal at UUNET, that's all I know," said David Takata, a Gruntal & Co analyst. UUNET, one of the largest Internet service providers and now owned by WorldCom Inc, is believed to have picked Ascend's networking products over Cisco Systems Inc's.
Ascend officials did not return calls.
A UUNet spokeswoman in Fairfax, Va. said she did not have any information about an impending deal with Ascend and said nothing has been announced.

Ascend CEO Mory Ejabat is believed to be traveling and meeting with investors to discuss the company's prospects. Ejabat was not in and did not return calls seeking comment, nor did Ascend chief financial officer Robert Dahl.
On Wednesday, Ascend's shares jumped 5-5/16 to 49-1/16 and it was the most heavily traded stock on the NASDAQ, with over 20 million shares changing hands.

Joseph Bellace, a Merrill Lynch analyst, upgraded Ascend Wednesday to accumulate from neutral, but no further details were available. On Tuesday, Montgomery Securities analyst Al Tobia made positive comments about its upcoming second quarter earnings.

On July 15, Ascend will report its second quarter earnings, which will for the first time include the results of its recent merger with Cascade Communications Corp, which closed on Monday. Also on Monday, Ascend restated its first quarter earnings to reflect the pooling of Cascade, which resulted in a loss of $0.88 a share.
